translation.title: Commentary on Sūrat "By the ʿAṣr." In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.

x: Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of God, glorified be His praise and hallowed be His names:
h
By the ʿaṣr (1) Indeed man is in loss (2) except those who believe and do righteous deeds and enjoin one another to the truth and enjoin one another to patience (3)
The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of His saying
h
By the ʿaṣr
Some said: it is an oath, and our Lord, exalted be His mention, swore by time (
i
al-dahr
). He said: al-ʿaṣr is time.
Mention of those who said this:

c: ʿAlī told me, he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ told us, he said: Muʿāwiya told me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
m: , he said: al-ʿaṣr is an hour of the hours of the day.

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from al-Ḥasan.
m: . He said: it is the evening (

x: The correct view on this question is to say that our Lord swore by al-ʿaṣr, and al-ʿaṣr is a name for time (
i
al-dahr

), which is the evening, the night and the day. He did not restrict what this name comprises to one meaning to the exclusion of another. Everything to which this name applies falls within what He swore by, glorified be His mention.
And His saying:
h
Indeed man is in loss
. He says: the son of Ādam is in ruin and diminution. ʿAlī ؓ used to recite it: "
i
Inna l-insāna la-fī khusrin, wa-innahu fīhi ilā ākhiri l-dahri
" ("Indeed man is in loss, and he is in it until the end of time"). [Fn 1]

c: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā [Fn 2] b. Wāṣil told me, he said: Abū Nuʿaym al-Faḍl b. Dukayn told us, he said: Isrāʾīl informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr Dhū Murr.
m: He said: I heard ʿAlī ؓ recite this word: "By the ʿaṣr and the misfortunes of time, indeed man is in loss, and he is in it until the end of time." [Fn 3]

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda.
m: . In some of the recitations [Fn 4]: "and he is in it until the end of time." [Fn 4]

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Wakīʿ told us, from Sufyān, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr Dhū Murr.
m: ʿAlī ؓ recited it: "By the ʿaṣr and the misfortunes of time, indeed man is in loss."

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us. And al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Waraqāʾ told us. Both [ʿĪsā and Waraqāʾ] from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid.

x: h
Except those who believe and do righteous deeds

. He says: except those who believed God, affirmed His oneness and acknowledged obedience to Him [Fn 6], did righteous deeds, fulfilled what was incumbent upon them of His obligations and avoided what He forbade them of acts of disobedience to Him. He excepted those who believed from "man" because
i
insān
has the sense of a plural, not of a singular. [Fn 6]

evidence.text: ʿAlī ؓ used to recite it: "*Inna l-insāna la-fī khusrin, wa-innahu fīhi ilā ākhiri l-dahri*" ("Indeed man is in loss, and he is in it until the end of time").
He said: I heard ʿAlī ؓ recite this word: "By the ʿaṣr and the misfortunes of time, indeed man is in loss, and he is in it until the end of time."
In some of the recitations [Fn 4]: "and he is in it until the end of time."
ʿAlī ؓ recited it: "By the ʿaṣr and the misfortunes of time, indeed man is in loss."

x: And His saying:
h
and enjoin one another to the truth
. He says: they charged one another to adhere to action in accordance with what God sent down in His Book of His commands, and to avoid what He forbade in it.
The people of interpretation said the same as we have said.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda.
m: and enjoin one another to the truth
: the truth is the Book of God. [Fn 1]

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from al-Ḥasan [Fn 2].
m: and enjoin one another to the truth
. He said: the truth is the Book of God. [Fn 3]

c: ʿImrān b. Bakkār al-Kalāʿī told me, he said: Khaṭṭāb b. ʿUthmān told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Sinān Abū Rawḥ al-Sakūnī told us, a Ḥimṣī whom I met in Armīniya.
m: He said: I heard al-Ḥasan say regarding
and enjoin one another to the truth
: the truth is the Book of God.

x: And His saying:
h
and enjoin one another to patience
. He says: they charged one another to be patient in acting in obedience to God.
The people of interpretation said the same as we have said.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda.
m: and enjoin one another to patience
. He said: patience is obedience to God. [Fn 1]

c: ʿImrān b. Bakkār al-Kalāʿī told me, he said: Khaṭṭāb b. ʿUthmān told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Sinān Abū Rawḥ told us.
m: He said: I heard al-Ḥasan say regarding His saying
and enjoin one another to patience

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from al-Ḥasan [Fn 2].
m: and enjoin one another to patience
. He said: patience is obedience to God. [Fn 1]

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzaq transmitted it in his Tafsir (2/394) from Maʿmar with this chain.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 394 عن معمر به.

notes.en: The reading is anomalous because it conflicts with the written form of the codex.
Manuscript M reads “Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla.” This is ʿAbd al-Aʿla ibn Wasil ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla; see Tahdhib al-Kamal (23/197).
notes.ar: في م: "ابن عبد الأعلى". وهو عبد الأعلى بن واصل بن عبد الأعلى، تهذيب الكمال 23/ 197.

notes.en: Al-Hakim transmitted it (2/534) through Israʾil with this chain. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/392) to al-Firyabi, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn al-Anbari in al-Masahif.
notes.ar: أخرجه الحاكم 2/ 534 من طريق إسرائيل به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 392 إلى الفريابي وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن الأنباري في المصاحف.

notes.en: Manuscripts S, T1, T2, and T3 read “the recitation.”
Tafsir Mujahid, p. 747; al-Firyabi transmitted it through Mujahid, as cited in Taghliq al-Taʿliq (4/4).
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 747، ومن طريقه الفريابي - كما في تغليق التعليق 4/ 4.

notes.en: Manuscript M reads “with oneness and obedience.”
Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/392) to ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 392 إلى عبد الرزاق وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzaq transmitted it in his Tafsir (2/394) from Maʿmar with this chain.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 394 عن معمر به.

notes.en: This is the continuation of the report cited on the preceding page.
notes.ar: تتمة الأثر المتقدم في الصفحة السابقة.
